content.value: Steam at $T _ { \alpha 1 } = 3 2 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ flows in a cast iron pipe $( k = 8 0 W / m . k )$ whose inner and outer diameters are $D _ { 1 } = 5 c m$ and $D _ { 2 } = 5 . 5 c m$ , respectively. The pipe is covered with 3 cm thick glass wool insulation with $k = 0 . 0 5 W / m .$ k. Heat is lost to the surroundings at $T _ { \alpha 2 } = 5 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ by natural convection andradiation, with a combined heat transfer coefficient of $h _ { 2 } =$ 18 $W / m ^ { 2 } . K$ . Taking the heat transfer coefficient inside the pipe to be $h _ { 1 } = 6 0 W / m ^ { 2 } . K ,$ determine the rate of heat loss from the steam per unit length of the pipe. Also, determine the temperature drops across the pipe shell and the insulation.
